title: Refresh an expiring vCenter session mid-run while applying a tag plan
prompt:
Platform automation ticket for our VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 estate. Build `VcfTagSync.psm1` at the workspace root. It must apply the desired-state tag plan in `tagplan.json` to the virtual machines of one vCenter, and it must survive the session token expiring partway through the run without losing or repeating work.

The runner already installs the PowerCLI SDK modules `VMware.Sdk.vSphere` 13.5.0.25380678 and `VMware.Sdk.vSphereRuntime` 8.0.2099.24145081. Import and use those genuine SDK modules: build the server configuration with `New-vSphereServerConfiguration`, issue every request with `Invoke-vSphereApiClient`, and build request payloads with the SDK models `Initialize-CisTaggingTagCreateSpec` and `Initialize-VapiStdDynamicID`. Do not vendor VMware modules or replace the SDK transport with `Invoke-WebRequest`, `Invoke-RestMethod`, curl, raw sockets, `HttpClient`, or another HTTP client.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a projection of `specifications/vsphere/openapi/automation/vcenter.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at tag `9.0.0.0`, the commit recorded in `docs/official_sources.json`. It comes from the specification, not a documentation page, and not the 9.1 revision of the same file. The only operationIds in scope are `Cis.Session_create`, `Cis.Session_delete`, `Vcenter.VM_list`, `Cis.Tagging.Category_list`, `Cis.Tagging.Category_get`, `Cis.Tagging.Tag_listTagsForCategory`, `Cis.Tagging.Tag_get`, `Cis.Tagging.Tag_create`, and `Cis.Tagging.TagAssociation_attachTagToMultipleObjects`. The acceptance harness points the real SDK at a contract-pinned loopback vCenter and calls:

`Invoke-VcfTagSync -Server <string> -Credential <pscredential> -PlanPath <string> [-SkipCertificateCheck]`

Requirements:

- Export only `Invoke-VcfTagSync`. `Server` is a `host:port` authority, and `SkipCertificateCheck` must reach the server configuration.
- Authenticate once with `Cis.Session_create` using the supplied credential over basic auth, then present the returned token as `vmware-api-session-id` on every later request. Log out with `Cis.Session_delete` when the plan is applied.
- Resolve every virtual machine named anywhere in the plan with a single `Vcenter.VM_list` request filtered on `names`. Every filter you did not set must be absent from the query string, not sent empty. Fail if vCenter does not list one of the planned machines.
- Resolve the plan's category by listing categories and reading each one until the name matches; the run must fail if that category does not exist, because creating categories is outside the contract. Then list the tags already in that category and read each one to learn its name.
- Create only the planned tags the category lacks, with `Cis.Tagging.Tag_create`. The specification makes `tag_id` optional: leave it unset so it is omitted from the body rather than sent as null or empty. Attach each assignment's tag to its machines in one `Cis.Tagging.TagAssociation_attachTagToMultipleObjects` request per assignment, and treat a batch result that is not successful as an error.
- The fixture token stops being accepted partway through the run and the request that hits the expiry comes back `401`. Detect that, create exactly one replacement session, and replay only the request that failed. Work that already succeeded must not be repeated, the spent token must not be used again, and the run must not open a session per request.
- The SDK runtime probes a pre-7.0.2 `/rest` endpoint when it is left to discover whether a server needs deprecated APIs. That endpoint is not in the contract, so pin the setting instead of letting it probe.
- Return an object with properties in this exact order: `Server`, `CategoryId`, `TagsCreated`, `VmsResolved`, `AttachedCount`, `SessionRefreshCount`. `TagsCreated` lists only the tags this run created, `VmsResolved` and `AttachedCount` are counts, and `SessionRefreshCount` counts replacement sessions.

Acceptance: `pwsh -NoProfile -File verify.ps1`. It uses dummy credentials against `127.0.0.1` only, invokes the genuine VMware SDK, and reads the mock's request log to verify the exact method, target, query shape, body member set, authorization, session lifecycle, replay of the rejected request, and omission of every unset optional field. No live VMware endpoint is contacted. `verify.ps1`, `mock_vcenter.py`, `tagplan.json`, `.gitignore`, and everything under `docs/` are protected; do not modify them.
